newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE shares end week mixed, index down.
newsitem.headline: UAE shares end week mixed, index down.

text.p: The 27-share index of the unofficial United Arab Emirates stock market ended the week to Thursday down for the first time in more than three months, brokers said.
The National Bank of Abu Dhabi (NBAD) 27-share index fell 2.5 points to 2,472.53, brokers said.

Brokers attributed the decline, which follows a period buoyed by company results, to a 20 dirham drop in Union National Bank's (UNB) share price to 340 dirhams from 360 the previous week. UNB, was 40 percent owned by Bank of Credit and Commerce (BCCI) before it collapsed with debts of more than $12 billion in 1991.
The share price gained more than 100 percent this year following reports of an imminent settlement to the BCCI case.
The government of Abu Dhabi, which was a majority shareholder in BCCI, acquired BCCI's 40 percent share in UNB as a result of a $1.55 billion settlement in May.
Brokers said UNB is expected to announce results this year for the first time in five years.

Abu Dhabi National Hotels Co was another loser this week, closing five dirhams lower at 1,045. Brokers attributed the decline to plans announced by Abu Dhabi on Wednesday to form a new joint stock company to acquire hotels and promote tourism.
Dubai Islamic Bank, Abu Dhabi National Insurance Company and Emirates Insurance Company gained five dirhams each to 185, 1,045 and 620 dirhams respectively.
Other share prices moved in a tight range.
